conviction_note: Fuel sets this print. Every peer that reported after Southwest's 22 July guide paid more for fuel than it had assumed: ALK $3.94/gal against $3.75, UAL $3.90 against $3.69, and Delta absorbed $500m above its early-July guide. Their Q4 assumptions are $4.25 (DAL, 9 Oct), $4.80 (UAL) and $4.65-4.85 (ALK). Southwest is unhedged after terminating its hedges, so its Q4 guide and its FY cut (FY consensus $2.88 already sits below the $3.25 guided floor) will likely be far below the July framework. Two things soften this. Sell-side Q3 EPS is already at $0.57, below the $0.625 guide midpoint after 16 downward revisions. And the sector's reaction function on 20-21 Oct was to buy a fuel-driven guide-down: UAL guided Q4 to a $1.00 midpoint against $1.88 consensus and rose ~5% after hours. Against that, LUV sold its last two guide-cut prints (-6.19%, -4.07%) and put skew is +3.7. The findings sum to about -0.2, the scaled number is -0.52, p_up 46, and the magnitude stays above the implied move because a guidance change is certain.

positioning_check: Short interest 24.54m shares, 5.06% of float, 3.5 days to cover, record date 2026-09-30, up 11.2% from 22.08m on 2026-09-15 (MarketBeat from FINRA, published 2026-10-09: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/LUV/short-interest/). Not a crowded short. Baseline: 25-delta skew +3.7 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.58, event-implied move 5.15%, straddle 5.48%. Spot $40.78 is +3.66% over 5 days, -0.63% over 20 days and 25.6% below the 52-week high; it rose about 2.7% on 2026-10-21 after UAL's print. Reaction history: 5 of the last 7 prints were down; the last two amc prints with guide cuts or no guide update were -6.19% and -4.07%; one +18.7% in Jan 2026. Same-window co-event: American Airlines reports Q3 before the open on 2026-10-22, inside LUV's window.

findings.finding: Q3 fuel very likely ran above Southwest's $3.70-3.75/gal guide assumption, which rested on the 17 July curve. Peers that reported after LUV last spoke came in over their own July assumptions by about $0.20: Alaska $3.94 against $3.75, United $3.90 against $3.69. On roughly 580m gallons a quarter (derived from the $889m Q2 y/y fuel increase), $0.20/gal is about $115m pre-tax, or about $0.17 of EPS before any fare recapture (UAL recaptured 72%). Net of recapture that is about $0.05-0.09 below the $0.625 guide midpoint, roughly onto the $0.57 consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 fuel came in below guide ($3.92 against $4.10-4.15) and adj EPS beat at $0.94 against about $0.51, yet the stock fell -6.19% on the FY guide cut. LUV has not paid for reported-quarter EPS surprises recently.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Q3 consensus is $0.57, below the $0.625 guide midpoint, after 16 down and 2 up revisions and a 3.4% drift down over 30 days. If the full fuel overrun were unpriced, consensus would still sit at or above the midpoint. What may remain is a residual of a few cents if Southwest's leisure-heavy domestic network recaptured less fuel through fares than UAL's.
findings.independence: UAL Q3 fuel of $3.90 against a $3.69 July assumption (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/ual-q3-earnings-miss-surging-121000795.html; July assumption at https://www.tikr.com/blog/united-airlines-guided-q3-below-the-street-the-fuel-price-behind-it-came-from-one-days-curve). Delta absorbed more than $500m of fuel above its early-July guide (https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx). LUV's assumption is from its Q2 8-K.

findings.finding: The Q4 guide and the FY cut will be set at a much higher fuel price than anything Southwest has guided on. Peers' Q4 all-in assumptions are $4.65-4.85 (ALK, 20 Oct, which guides a Q4 loss of $2.00-2.50/share), about $4.80 (UAL, against Q3's $3.90) and about $4.25 (DAL on 9 Oct, before Brent reached $110 on 19 Oct). Southwest is unhedged after terminating its contracts. FY consensus of $2.88 already sits below the $3.25-4.25 guided floor, so the cut itself is expected. The open question is how far the Q4 guide falls below a consensus that is itself unsourced: about $0.9 is only implied by FY $2.88 less Q1 $0.45, Q2 $0.94 and Q3 $0.57. Each extra $0.50/gal on about 580m gallons is roughly $0.45/share.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is what moves LUV. Jul 2026: FY cut from at least $4.00 to $3.25-4.25 on a large beat, -6.19%. Apr 2026: declined to update the $4.00 FY guide, -4.07%. Jan 2026: the new-model guide drove +18.7%. Peers this month: DAL fell about 3% on its FY cut (9 Oct); UAL rose about 4.8% after hours on a Q4 midpoint of $1.00 against $1.88 consensus (20 Oct).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. FY consensus is already below the guide floor, Brent at $110 is public, put skew is +3.7, and LUV trades 25.6% below its 52-week high. What could be unpriced is the Q4 number: peers' consensus was stale by 40-50% on Q4 (UAL $1.00 midpoint against $1.88). If LUV's Q4 consensus has not caught up, the guide lands far below it. If the market had fully priced this, LUV would not have rallied 3.7% over 5 days into the print.
findings.independence: UAL Q4 fuel of $4.80 and guide of $0.50-1.50 against $1.75-1.88 consensus (https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/united-airlines-falls-on-weak-fourth-quarter-guidance-4960956; https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/ual-q3-earnings-miss-surging-121000795.html). Delta Q4 fuel of $4.25 and guide of $1.15-1.65 against $1.86 a year earlier (https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx). Wholesale jet fuel of about $4.95/gal in NY on 10 Oct (Bloomberg via search snippet, https://www.globalair.com/articles/aviation-fuel-spotlight-oil-is-flowing-but-jet-a-didnt-get-the-memo/12728, snippet_only). Brent reached $110 on 19 Oct (247wallst, 2026-10-21). The FY consensus figure shares the 247wallst document with the bar.

findings.finding: The sector's reaction function this week has been to buy fuel-driven guide-downs when demand holds. United guided Q4 EPS to $0.50-1.50 against about $1.88 consensus, said it is 'highly confident' of recapturing 100% of fuel with a lag, and saw sell-in yields up high-teens. Its shares rose about 4.8% after hours on 20 Oct (to $102.51 from $97.77) and were up again on 21 Oct. LUV rose about 2.7% intraday on 21 Oct in sympathy (24/7 Wall St widget, $39.55 to $40.74; baseline spot $40.78).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This line cuts against LUV's own history: its last two guide cuts were sold (-6.19%, -4.07%). Among peers this month, DAL's cut was sold about 3% (9 Oct) and UAL's was bought about 5% (20-21 Oct). ALK's reaction to its 20 Oct loss guide was not found.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: LUV has already rallied about 3.7% over 5 days, most of it on 21 Oct. The UAL template suggests investors are anchored on recapture with a lag rather than on Q4 EPS, so a Q4 guide far below a stale consensus may not be sold as hard as the July cut was. If this were fully in the price, the skew would have flattened from +3.7.
findings.independence: Same UAL event as the price data in https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/united-airlines-falls-on-weak-fourth-quarter-guidance-4960956 (shares up in early trading 21 Oct). TD Cowen called UAL's consensus 'irrelevant' and weakness a buying opportunity (same article). Counter-case: DAL's 9 Oct cut was sold about 3% (rttnews).

findings.finding: Network carriers are adding domestic seats into Q4: an analyst on UAL's Q3 call said United and American each plan roughly 8-9% domestic capacity growth in Q4. That is pressure on Southwest's all-domestic RASM just as it needs fares to recapture fuel. UAL's CEO separately expects 6-10 US airlines to lose money this year and 'supply changes' if oil stays high.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No LUV-specific history on competitor capacity commentary found. In 2024-25 LUV's RASM guides were cut on domestic capacity glut episodes, but no source was retrieved here, so treat that as context only.
findings.why_not_priced: Schedule data is public to airline analysts, so this is likely mostly priced. It reaches LUV's guide only if management cites competitive pressure in the Q4 RASM range. If it were unpriced, LUV would have lagged UAL on 21 Oct, and it did not.
findings.independence: A proxy: an analyst's statement on another airline's call, not confirmed by Southwest. Shares the UAL transcript document with the positioning finding.

findings.finding: Peer unit revenue in Q3 was strong and above guides, which supports Southwest landing at or above the top of its +17.5-19.5% RASM guide. ALK RASM was +11.7% against 'low double digits' guided, with September yield up about 17%. UAL TRASM was +15.9% (best since the pandemic) and domestic PRASM +14.5%. DAL domestic unit revenue was +16%. LUV's comparison also gets assigned seating (live from 27 Jan 2026, so a y/y benefit through Q4), and Spirit's exit on 2 May 2026 removed about 21.3m seats May-Dec, concentrated at FLL, MCO, LAS and HOU, which are Southwest-heavy airports.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: adj RASM +20.1%, above guide, yet the stock fell -6.19% because the guide set the move. A RASM beat inside the guided band has not paid on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: Revenue consensus of $8.24B (+18.6%) already sits near the guide midpoint, so a top-of-range RASM is worth about +0.5% on revenue. The value is mainly what it implies for Q4 fare recapture: the Q4 RASM guide would be visibly higher than a +18% repeat. Spirit's exit is five months old and priced.
findings.independence: UAL (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/ual-q3-earnings-miss-surging-121000795.html); DAL (https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx); Spirit shutdown 2 May 2026 (https://katv.com/news/nation-world/spirit-shutdown-fl-based-budget-airline-ceases-operations-after-failed-federal-buyout). All are peer proxies; Southwest has given no Q3 RASM update since July.

findings.finding: The buyback has stopped. Southwest repurchased nothing in Q2 2026, against $1.5B in Q2 2025, after $1.25B in H1, and only $450m remains on the $2.0B authorization. With an unhedged fuel bill rising in Q4, a restart announced with the print is unlikely, so per-share support from repurchases is gone for now.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not isolable. The Sept 2024 $2.5B buyback announcement was a positive catalyst, but it came outside a print.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it was disclosed in July. It matters only if the release confirms no Q3 repurchases or withdraws the remaining authorization.

findings.finding: The August 2026 8-Ks show a new $2B five-year revolver (accordion to $3B, undrawn, replacing a 2016 facility, 10 Aug), two new directors, and executive pay raised to peer levels citing 'heightened risk of losing key senior executive talent'. Liquidity was $5.3B at Q2 with gross leverage 2.1x.
findings.why_not_priced: Asked what the money buys: an undrawn standby facility replacing an old one, which is routine liquidity backup and not distress. With fuel elevated it is a mild comfort rather than a negative. It has been public since August.

outside_window.finding: UAL management expects fuel to stay elevated through 2027 and that 2027 industry capacity plans are not firm; supply cuts by loss-making carriers would be a medium-term tailwind for Southwest's domestic yields.

baseline_tension: The negatives (fuel above assumption, a Q4 guide set at $4.65-4.85/gal fuel) agree with the +3.7 put skew and with LUV's habit of selling guide cuts, so they are probably priced. The one thing cutting against the skew is the sector's reaction to UAL's guide-down this week, which LUV has already partly ridden (+3.7% over 5 days). Net, p_up is held near 50 at 46.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction) and rule 6 (inside the guide): the Q3 fuel finding was cut from -0.6 to -0.4, because consensus already sits below the guide midpoint and LUV sold its last big EPS beat.
Rule 6 (unsourced bar): the Q4/FY guidance finding was capped from -1.0 to -0.7, because the Q4 consensus is only derived and the FY $2.88 has one source.
Rule 5 (proxy): the competitor-capacity finding was trimmed from -0.4 to -0.3, as an analyst proxy on another airline's call.

Rule 7 (positioning): short interest of 5.06% with 3.5 days to cover is not crowded, so the negatives were not shrunk further for a squeeze. The negatives agree with the skew, which keeps p_up near 50.
Rule 4 (financing): the revolver was checked against what it buys (an undrawn backup replacing a 2016 facility) and left at 0.
'Asking what the market missed generates pessimism': the draft's negative lean was checked against the positive UAL reaction-function finding, which was left at +0.7.
